study type: Birth cohort study (baseline data collected cross-sectionally)
exposure: Newborn breastfeeding in the first hour of life
outcome: Maternal demographic characteristics (e.g., average education, adolescent mothers)
Maternal health behaviors (e.g., smoking rates, prenatal care adherence)
Newborn health status (e.g., prevalence of low birth weight, preterm birth rates)
Newborn characteristics (e.g., sex, length, head circumference)
Newborn feeding practices (e.g., rates of breastfeeding in the first hour of life)
cohort: The study included 1181 mother-child pairs recruited at a University Hospital's maternity in Canoas, Brazil.
finding: Baseline data revealed a reasonable proportion of mothers with low levels of education and smokers, and a high proportion of maternal comorbidities and cesarean deliveries, along with a significant rate of preterm births and low birth weight.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery represented 43.2% of births in the study cohort.
cross-section timing: Data was collected cross-sectionally at the University Hospital's maternity, likely around the time of birth.
birth_weight: Birth weight was collected for all newborns, with a prevalence of low birth weight at 6.3%.
gest_age: Gestational age was collected, with 27.7% of pregnancies not reaching 37 weeks.
